purpose: Single-lane A/B/C/A release comparison: baseline, priority abandonment, 128 KiB fresh-source admission, baseline. Both candidates remain isolated.
kernel: Linux 6.8.0-149-generic #149-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Oct 23 13:21:10 UTC 2026 x86_64
cpu_model: model name	: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6138 CPU @ 2.00GHz
instrumentation: Ordinary counters only; no timing instrumentation or controller override.
single_lane_harness: benches/tap_transport.sh with only tx_lanes = $workers replaced by tx_lanes = 1; workers and TAP queues remain eight

priority.validation: 351 ordinary release tests, strict Clippy and formatting; 90 kernel tests on Linux 6.8 and 7.0; three unchanged runtime tests passed.

admission_128k.validation: 349 ordinary release tests, strict Clippy and formatting; 80 kernel and three unchanged runtime tests on both Linux 6.8 and 7.0. Allocation assertions unchanged.

limitations: One sequential A/B/C/A series; the two candidates share the same controls, rather than separate adjacent A/B/A sequences.
Twenty-second points; no claim of a universal plateau or CPU ceiling.
128 KiB admission fails low-rate synchronized bursts and is rejected despite its overload improvement.
Priority abandonment still falls from its 4 Gbit/s point; eight-lane performance not measured here.
No local builds, kernel tests or Git packing overlapped load. Remote Linux 7 tests used a separate host.
One inner UDP receive error at the 128 KiB candidate's 21 Gbit/s point; zero outer socket overflow, corruption, duplicates or outer fragmentation throughout.
